messages:
Maria (AM): kicking off FinTrust POC thread. They need Redwood Private in their AWS account, must complete security questionnaire, and require deterministic egress IPs for allowlisting. Timeline: 2-week POC.
Alex (SE): primary asks: preserve client source IP for downstream services and support mTLS to control plane. They asked for guidance: PrivateLink vs VPC Peering.
Raj (NetOps): PrivateLink (interface endpoints) is preferred: avoids route-table exposure, provides stable DNS endpoints, and avoids overlapping-CIDR peering issues. Peering can work but has limitations for cross-account and overlapping CIDRs.
Maria (AM): two blockers from the security questionnaire: 1) rotating/unknown egress IPs, 2) need explicit firewall rules for management/control plane.
Tim (Solutions Eng): recommended patterns:
- Minimal POC: use existing NAT in customer account (cheapest) -> outgoing SNAT; loses client IP.
- Full-preservation: run Redwood Private in customer VPC behind NLBs with proxy-protocol v2 OR use NLB with EIPs + NAT Gateway per AZ for stable egress IPs.
Example snippet for customer doc:
```
Deploy NLB(s) in private subnets -> serve traffic to instances/pods
Use proxy-protocol v2 on NLB to preserve client IP
For stable egress: provision NAT Gateway(s) with EIPs per AZ
```
Raj (NetOps): test for PrivateLink connectivity:
```
curl -v https://vpce-012345-abc.vpce-svc-xxxx.us-west-2.vpce.amazonaws.com/health -H 'Host: model.redwood-inference.com'
```
Alex (SE): note on TLS inspection: if customer does TLS/TCP proxying that rewrites SNI, this will break cert validation. Recommend either bypass for our hostnames or use mTLS to avoid MITM.
Sophia (InfoSec): security wording for questionnaire: "No inbound internet ports required. Outbound: HTTPS (443) to control plane FQDNs (*.redwood-inference.com). For allowlist, customer can use dedicated EIPs/NAT Gateways; TLS 1.2+ enforced; customer-managed KMS supported for Private deployments; key usage auditable via CloudTrail."
Maria (AM): pricing Q: will dedicated EIPs/NAT add to POC cost?
Tim (Solutions Eng): yes. Present two POC cost options: Minimal (reuse existing NAT, lower infra $) vs Isolated (NAT Gateway + EIPs per AZ, higher infra $). Provide ballpark NAT Gateway cost per AZ and EIP charge in the quote.
Alex (SE): model pull/update requirements: outbound HTTPS to s3.amazonaws.com or our model registry endpoints for model blobs. Recommend customers allow FQDNs; if IPs required, provide EIP list.
Raj (NetOps): warning: VPC Peering with overlapping CIDRs can route incorrectly between spokes. If they have complex topologies, recommend Transit Gateway or PrivateLink.
Tim (Solutions Eng): Maria asked for a one-page network diagram. I'll post PNG + ASCII fallback showing: customer VPC -> private subnets -> NLB -> serving plane -> NAT + EIPs for egress -> interface endpoints (PrivateLink) and arrows to S3/KMS. ETA: today.
Sophia (InfoSec): I'll draft the attestation snippet and link SOC2/ISO certs. ETA: tomorrow.
Maria (AM): action items: 1) Tim: one-page diagram + curl test (ETA today), 2) Raj: suggested firewall rules & NAT/EIP pattern (ETA EOD), 3) Sophia: questionnaire attestation wording (ETA tomorrow), 4) Alex: KMS options note for legal.
deploy-bot: POC sandbox infra ready in us-west-2 (build-982). :rocket:
Maria (AM): thanks, will present to FinTrust tomorrow. Add any one-line clarifications below.
Alex (SE): one-liner for questionnaire: "Control plane traffic uses TLS 1.2+ to public FQDNs; customers can enforce egress via dedicated EIPs for allowlisting."
Sophia (InfoSec): and: "Customer-managed KMS supported; key usage auditable via CloudTrail."
Maria (AM): closing loop. I'll attach the diagram to the questionnaire.
